verses.23:1: Do Senhor é a terra, e {plenitudo}: * {orbis}, e todos os que nele habitam.
verses.23:2: {ipse} sobre os mares: * e o preparou sobre os rios.
verses.23:3: Quem subirá ao monte do Senhor? * ou quem {stabit} no seu lugar santo?
verses.23:4: {innocens}, * que não {accepit} em vão a sua alma, {dolo}.
verses.23:5: Este {accipiet} a bênção do Senhor: * e a misericórdia de Deus, {salutari}.
verses.23:6: Esta é a geração dos que o buscam, * dos que buscam a face do Deus de Jacó.
verses.23:7: {attollite}, e {elevamini}, portas {aeternales}: * e entrará o Rei da glória.
verses.23:8: Quem é este Rei da glória? * O Senhor forte e poderoso: o Senhor poderoso na batalha.
verses.23:9: {attollite}, e {elevamini}, portas {aeternales}: * e entrará o Rei da glória.
verses.23:10: Quem é este Rei da glória? * O Senhor {virtutum}, {ipseest} o Rei da glória.

decisions.why: plenitúdo: 'fulness' (τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς) — all that fills the earth. The formula returns 'terra / mare / orbis … et plenitúdo ejus' in 49:12, 88:12, 95:11, 97:6 (grep), so one wording should serve all five. St Paul quotes the half-verse word for word (1 Cor 10:26 'Domini est terra, et plenitudo ejus', Clementine fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-46-10.json). Douay-Rheims 'the fulness thereof'; Matos Soares 1932 'e tudo que ela encerra' (a paraphrase).

options.label: a sua plenitude
options.note: Ruling: the noun kept, current Portuguese; the possessive after 'a terra' points to it.

options.label: tudo o que ela contém
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense ('tudo que ela encerra'): the noun explained as a clause — refused (rule 2).

decisions.why: D30: orbis terræ / terrárum → 'o mundo' in all its lines (the row names 23:1). 'mundo' is masculine, as orbis is, so 'nele' (in eo) and, in 23:2, 'o fundou … o preparou' (eum) point to it as the Latin's pronouns point to orbis, not to terra.

options.label: o mundo
options.note: Ruling: D30.

options.label: o orbe da terra
options.note: Both Latin words; 'orbe' unknown to two blind readers (Pss 9, 17).

decisions.latin: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum
decisions.why: ipse: 'he himself', an emphatic subject; eum (masculine) is orbis — the world, 'o mundo' of 23:1. The Hebrew-family pronoun is feminine (the earth); the Latin's masculine is followed, which 'o mundo' makes possible. fundáre → fundar, præparáre → preparar (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'For he hath founded it upon the seas'; Matos Soares 1932 'Porque ele a fundou' (feminine, the earth).

options.label: Porque ele o fundou
options.note: Ruling: the subject named; the Latin's emphasis carried by stress, not by an added word.

options.label: Porque foi ele que o fundou

forms.ipse: Porque foi ele que o fundou

options.note: ipse's emphasis as a cleft; two syllables heavier.

options.label: Porque ele mesmo o fundou
options.note: ipse to the letter; 'mesmo' is heard as 'even'.

decisions.latin: aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
decisions.why: stare → estar de pé (glossary, open; 133:1b, 17:39): to stand in the holy place, as the priests 'qui statis in domo Dómini'. The question answers the one before it (who goes up, who stands). Douay-Rheims 'who shall stand'; Matos Soares 1932 'quem estará'. in loco sancto → 'no seu lugar santo' (glossary sanctum, a place).

options.label: estará de pé
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's stare.

options.label: permanecerá
options.note: Standing as remaining; permanére's verb in this psalter.

options.label: estará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the posture lost.

decisions.why: The answer opens with two adjectives with ablatives of respect ('innocent in hands and clean of heart'; ἀθῷος χερσὶν καὶ καθαρὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ). mundus → puro (D30's note: 'puro' is what mundus 'clean' becomes). 'puro de coração' is the Beatitude's phrase in the Brazilian ear. The Monday Prime antiphon adapts the verse: 'Ínnocens mánibus * et mundo corde ascéndet in montem Dómini' (Psalterium/Psalmi/Psalmi minor.txt) — the wording must carry that too ('O inocente de mãos e puro de coração subirá ao monte do Senhor'). Ps 14, this psalm's cousin, answered its 'quis?' with 'Aquele que …' because there the Latin has 'Qui'; here it has an adjective. Douay-Rheims 'The innocent in hands, and clean of heart'; Matos Soares 1932 'O inocente de mãos e limpo de coração'.

options.label: O inocente de mãos e puro de coração

forms.innocens: O inocente de mãos e puro de coração

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's two adjectives, parallel as the Latin; Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 build it so.

options.label: Aquele que tem mãos inocentes e coração puro

forms.innocens: Aquele que tem mãos inocentes e coração puro

options.note: Ps 14's answer, with a verb supplied; more natural, the adjectives turned into nouns' qualities.

options.label: O de mãos inocentes e de coração puro

forms.innocens: O de mãos inocentes e de coração puro

options.note: The ablatives as 'de' phrases; a clipped build.

decisions.latin: qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam … Hic accípiet benedictiónem
decisions.why: One verb twice, two verses apart: accépit … accípiet (ἔλαβεν … λήμψεται, the Greek too). The Latin sets the man who did not take/receive his soul 'in vano' beside the man who will take/receive a blessing — the repetition is kept (rule 2) with one verb. 'receber' serves both; 'tomar' (17:17 'me tomou') would give the commandment's idiom 'tomar em vão' in 23:4 (Douay-Rheims 'taken his soul in vain') but 'tomará a bênção' in 23:5 is not said. What 'receive one's soul in vain' means is left as open as the Latin (a life received for nothing, or a soul given to vanity). Matos Soares 1932 'o que não entregou à vaidade a sua alma' explains, and drops the repetition ('receberá' in 23:5).

options.label: recebeu … receberá
options.note: Ruling: one verb for the Latin's one, the repetition heard.

options.label: tomou … receberá
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'taken … receive': the catechism's 'tomar em vão' in 23:4; the repetition lost.

options.label: tomou … tomará
options.note: One verb, 'tomar' (17:17): 'tomará a bênção' is not Portuguese.

options.label: entregou à vaidade … receberá
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's sense (the verse then reads 'não entregou em vão'): explains — refused (rule 2).

decisions.latin: nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo
decisions.why: The glossary row dolus pencilled this colon as 'nem jurou com engano ao seu próximo' (from Ps 14's agent). Rule 4 moves the words: 'próximo' is a proparoxytone and would close the verse (the glossary's próximo row: 'at a cadence it needs a word after it'), where the Latin closes on 'suo'. The dative first, the manner last: 'nem jurou ao seu próximo com engano' ends on a paroxytone. Nothing else changes. Douay-Rheims 'nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour'; Matos Soares 1932 'nem fez juramentos dolosos ao seu próximo'.

options.label: nem jurou ao seu próximo com engano

forms.dolo: nem jurou ao seu próximo com engano

options.note: Ruling: the glossary's words, reordered for the cadence (rule 4).

options.label: nem jurou com engano ao seu próximo

forms.dolo: nem jurou com engano ao seu próximo

options.note: The glossary's pencilled order: the verse ends on a proparoxytone.

decisions.why: salutári is the ablative of salutáris used as a title in apposition to Deo: 'from God his saving one' — the Greek σωτῆρος αὐτοῦ, 'his Saviour'; 'Deus salutáris noster' is a formula of the psalter (64:6, 78:9, 84:5). The form could also be the neuter noun salutáre (→ salvação, D6), but in apposition to a person and with the Greek's σωτήρ the title is the reading of both Vulgate-family versions (Douay-Rheims 'God his Saviour'; Matos Soares 1932 'Deus, seu Salvador'). Cost: Ps 24:5 has salvátor ('salvátor meus', σωτήρ too), and both become 'Salvador' — one Greek word, D15's test allows the merge.

options.label: seu Salvador
options.note: Ruling: the title (the Greek σωτῆρος); both Vulgate-family versions.

options.label: sua salvação
options.note: D6's word for the neuter salutáre, which the form allows; keeps salutáris apart from salvátor (24:5), but makes God a 'salvation' where the Greek names a saviour.

decisions.why: 23:7 and 23:9 are one Latin line, sung in dialogue with 23:8 and 23:10; both verses are built from the same slots so that they cannot drift. attóllere: 'lift up, raise' — only these two lines (grep). Two Latin verbs in the line (attóllite … elevámini) stay two: levantar is leváre's (24:1 'levávi ánimam meam', 118:48, 120:1), elevar is eleváre's (8:2b 'se elevou'), so attóllere takes 'erguer' — free in the glossary but for extóllere (open, 133:2), which never meets it. 'Erguei' is safe at the vós imperative (past 'ergui'). The vocative 'príncipes' stays in the middle as the Latin has it (Douay-Rheims 'Lift up your gates, O ye princes'; Matos Soares 1932 'Levantai, ó príncipes, as vossas portas'); no 'ó', which the Latin does not have. The line is sung at Advent: DO's first Sunday of Advent has 'V. Tóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini portæ æternáles, et introíbit Rex glóriæ' (Tempora/Adv1-0.txt; the text of the Roman Missal family, with Tóllite) — not this psalm's Latin, but the Portuguese should serve it.

options.label: Erguei, príncipes, as vossas portas
options.note: Ruling: a verb of its own for attóllere; the Latin's order.

options.label: Levantai, ó príncipes, as vossas portas

forms.attollite: Levantai, ó príncipes, as vossas portas

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the familiar sound; 'levantar' is leváre's, and 'ó' is added.

options.label: Príncipes, erguei as vossas portas
options.note: The vocative first, natural order; the verb no longer opens the line as the Latin's does.

decisions.why: elevámini: passive imperative of eleváre with middle sense (ἐπάρθητε), said to the gates themselves. The glossary's eleváre (passive) → elevar-se (8:2b 'se elevou') and the pronominal imperative of Exaltáre → 'exaltai-vos' (7:7a) give 'elevai-vos' (safe: past 'elevei'). Douay-Rheims 'be ye lifted up'; Matos Soares 1932 'levantai-vos' (one verb for the Latin's two).

options.label: elevai-vos
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's pronominal form for the middle passive.

options.label: sede elevadas
options.note: The passive to the letter (as the option 'sede exaltado' in 7:7a).

options.label: levantai-vos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: merges the Latin's two verbs.

decisions.why: æternális: 'eternal' (πύλαι αἰώνιοι). Matos Soares 1932 keeps 'portas eternas' and adds a note that the phrase is a hyperbole for 'very ancient gates' — the Hebrew's sense (pitḥê 'ôlām). The Latin says eternal; the Fathers heard the gates of heaven opening to the ascending Christ (St Ambrose, read at the Ascension in DO, Tempora/Pasc6-3.txt, quotes the verse so). Kept.

options.label: eternas
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word (Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932).

options.label: antigas
options.note: The Hebrew's sense, as Matos Soares 1932's note explains it — refused (rule 1).

decisions.why: Dóminus virtútum is the Greek's κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων ('Lord of the powers'), which renders the Hebrew's Sabaoth. It is a formula of the psalter: 16 lines (45:8, 45:12, 47:9, 58:6, 67:13 Rex virtútum, 68:7, 79:5, 8, 15, 20, 83:2, 4, 9, 13, 88:9 — grep); this is its first place. The glossary's virtus → poder (open) and 20:14b's plural 'os vossos poderes' give 'o Senhor dos poderes' — the Latin's noun, heard as the powers of heaven and of battle together. Douay-Rheims 'the Lord of hosts' (the Hebrew's sense, via the English Bible); Matos Soares 1932 'O Senhor das virtudes' (the cognate — 'virtudes' are moral qualities in Brazil, or one of the angelic choirs). A glossary row is proposed.

options.label: dos poderes
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's virtus → poder, plural as 20:14b.

options.label: dos exércitos
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'hosts' and the Hebrew's Sabaoth: the familiar sense, not the Latin's word.

options.label: das virtudes
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the cognate, heard as moral virtues.

decisions.why: ipse emphatic: 'he, and no other, is the King of glory' — the answer to the question, closing the dialogue. Portuguese marks the emphasis by putting the verb first ('é ele'), which the ear hears as the answer. Douay-Rheims 'he is the King of Glory'; Matos Soares 1932 'esse é o Rei da glória'.

options.label: é ele
options.note: Ruling: the emphasis by order.

options.label: ele é
options.note: Plain order; the emphasis flattens.

options.label: esse é
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: a demonstrative pointing back.

choices.23:1: Dómini est terra → 'Do Senhor é a terra' (the Latin's order, good Portuguese; = 1 Cor 10:26, fetched). univérsi → 'todos' (glossary univérsus).
choices.23:3: ascéndere → subir. in montem Dómini → 'ao monte do Senhor'.
choices.23:5: benedíctio → bênção (glossary). 'a Dómino … a Deo' → 'do Senhor … de Deus'.
choices.23:6: quǽrere → buscar (glossary), twice as the Latin. generátio → geração. Dei Jacob → 'do Deus de Jacó'.
choices.23:7: introíre → entrar (íngredi / intráre → entrar). 'Rex glóriæ' → 'o Rei da glória', capital as 'Rei' is elsewhere (5:3). No 'ó' before the vocatives: the Latin has none.
choices.23:8: fortis et potens … potens → 'forte e poderoso … poderoso', the repetition kept. prǽlium → batalha (17:35).
choices.23:9: Built from the same slots as 23:7: the two cannot differ.
choices.23:10: The question is 23:8's word for word.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm23.txt, ten prayed verses, ids 23:1–23:10 (none repeated). No titulus (D7; the Greek's 'τῆς μιᾶς σαββάτων' is not in DO's text). DO's other uses checked by grep: the Monday Prime antiphon 'Ínnocens mánibus * et mundo corde ascéndet in montem Dómini' (Psalmi minor.txt); 'Tóllite portas' (a different Latin text) as the Advent I versicle (Tempora/Adv1-0.txt), an antiphon (Commune/C8.txt) and C10a; St Ambrose's reading at the Ascension quotes 23:7 (Tempora/Pasc6-3.txt). 1 Cor 10:26 quotes 23:1a word for word (Clementine, consult/bolls-VULG-46-10.json).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps023.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932; no Diurnal text for this psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: plenitúdo (5 lines), attóllere (2: 23:7, 23:9 only), elevámini (2), prǽlium (5), accípere (10), in vano (3), Dóminus / Deus virtútum (16). Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 23:1 'o mundo … nele' and 23:2 'o fundou … o preparou' (the Latin's masculine orbis, not the earth), 23:4 'não recebeu em vão a sua alma' (not 'lifted up his soul to what is false'; the Latin's verb), 23:5 'a misericórdia' (not 'justice'), 23:6 'a face do Deus de Jacó' (the Latin and Greek, not the Hebrew's 'your face, Jacob'), 23:7 'elevai-vos, portas eternas' (not 'ancient doors'), 23:10 'o Senhor dos poderes' (the Latin's noun). 23:7 = 23:9 from the same slots. 13 decisions.
